item.title: Fri Oct 9: Perturb-seq operators that don't generalize, asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos, and temperature-robust morphogen gradients
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Additive-input encoding fails operator-level target-held-out prediction on current Perturb-seq screens — Fullmer, K. et al.
    A rigorous negative result showing that fixed additive-input linear operators fail to generalize to held-out perturbation targets in Perturb-seq screens, directly challenging a common modeling assumption underlying GRN inference from perturbation data.
  2. Lineage tracing reveals asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos and stem cell-derived embryo models — Liu, Y. et al.
    Combining DNA Typewriter lineage recording with tetraploid complementation to build high-resolution single-cell genealogies reveals that fate restriction in mouse embryos is progressive and asynchronous, with cell identity alone failing to predict lineage history.
  3. Predictive Multiplicity in Cell-Fate Assignment: Label-Free Rashomon Sets and the Limits of Per-Cell Certification — Arjun Bhupatiraju et al.
    A careful statistical dissection of predictive multiplicity in trajectory inference shows that label-free Rashomon-set certification does not improve per-cell fate-assignment reliability over a model's own confidence, a cautionary methodological result for the single-cell trajectory field.
  4. Temperature scaling of developmental tempo reveals reaction-dominated morphogen patterning — Capek, D. et al.
    Elegant quantitative developmental biology showing that morphogen gradients in medaka embryos remain correctly scaled across temperature-driven changes in developmental tempo because patterning operates in a reaction-dominated regime rather than a diffusion-dominated one.
  5. Protein Language Model-Conditioned Graph Neural Networks for Multitask GPCR Ligand Activity Prediction — De, M. et al.
    AmbiDose introduces per-cell, expression-aware removal budgets for ambient RNA contamination in droplet scRNA-seq, substantially outperforming existing decontamination approaches on cross-species and marker-leakage benchmarks.

Briefs

  1. STAVelo: deciphering spatiotemporal cellular dynamics via spatial RNA velocity inference from spatial transcriptomics data — Li, S. et al.
    STAVelo extends RNA velocity to spatial transcriptomics with a graph-attention model, accurately recovering spatial developmental gradients across brain, kidney, heart and placenta datasets.
  2. HyperCom: a hypergraph-based method to infer cell-resolved cell-cell communication — Moy, J. K. et al.
    HyperCom uses hypergraph diffusion to infer cell-resolved, rather than cell-type-aggregated, ligand-receptor communication, reducing a common source of bias in cell-cell communication analysis.
  3. scStable: assessing scRNA-seq analysis stability under bulk-derived between-sample variation — Jiang, C. et al.
    scStable injects bulk-derived between-sample variation into single-sample scRNA-seq references to assess discovery stability, addressing the common but under-tested problem of single-sample scRNA-seq generalizability.
  4. PHC2-Dependent PRC1 Assemblies Stabilize Motor Neuron Hox Codes — Miller, A. K. et al.
    Shows that PHC2-dependent PRC1 subnuclear condensates are required to stabilize Hox transcriptional boundaries and motor neuron segmental identity, linking chromatin 3D assembly to gene regulatory output.
  5. Heterochromatin protein 1α acts as an essential stabilizer of chromatin packing domains — Kuo, T. et al.
    Demonstrates that HP1 alpha crosslinking is essential for maintaining heterochromatic cores of chromatin packing domains and for enabling stress-responsive transcriptional reprogramming.
  6. Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants — Pratik Dutta et al.
    ARGUS pairs 458 DNABERT TF-binding models with an LLM-mediated evidence-gathering agent to interpret noncoding GWAS variants, showing how uncertainty-aware tool orchestration can resolve conflicting regulatory evidence without hallucination.
  7. A gene-centric analysis of copy number variation reveals tumour suppressor modulation of cancer risk and novel associations with common diseases — Matthews, S. et al.
    A gene-centric, rather than region-based, CNV analysis identifies novel whole-gene deletions, including a germline extension of the 13q14 somatic association, linked to cancer risk and other common diseases.
  8. Robust ORF Deconvolution from Multiple Ribo-seq Datasets with Group LASSO Penalty — Maidhof, K. et al.
    PRICE 2 applies group-LASSO deconvolution across multiple Ribo-seq datasets to resolve weakly translated and overlapping ORFs, substantially boosting discovery of cryptic MHC-I peptide sources.
  9. Dynamic Schlafen 11 (SLFN11) expression revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing of clonal human cancer cells — Taniyama, D. et al.
    Single-cell profiling reveals dynamic, heterogeneous SLFN11 expression linked to a stress-response state, exposing a hidden determinant of chemotherapy resistance invisible to bulk assays.
  10. Limitations of Genomic Foundation Models for Decoding Regulatory Mechanisms in ALS — Talukder, A. et al.
    A sobering benchmark showing that AlphaGenome fails to recover measured splicing QTL effect sizes and effector genes in ALS, highlighting current limits of genomic foundation models for regulatory variant interpretation.

Quick mentions

  1. Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes — Faure, R. et al.
    Releases experiment-wide sketches and an all-pairs similarity matrix for 4.8 million SRA metagenomes, enabling unprecedented scale metagenome comparison and metadata correction.
  2. Inhibitory Nectin-2/TIGIT interactions between CD163+ macrophages and CD8+ T cells in spatially defined immune niches associate with poor outcomes in neuroblastoma — Borst, A. L. et al.
    Spatial imaging mass cytometry identifies CD163+ macrophage-CD8+ T cell Nectin-2/TIGIT interactions in immune niches that correlate with poor neuroblastoma outcomes.
  3. Beyond Action Entropy: Quotient-Space Exploration for Genome-Scale Metabolic Model Repair — Xuan Gong et al.
    QuotientPO reframes genome-scale metabolic model repair as quotient-space exploration over mechanistically equivalent edits, improving mechanism-level discovery under verifier-induced equivalence.
  4. CCT2 expression marks a translation-activated state in sporadic ALS motor neurons and is associated with functional decline — Bhandary, P. et al.
    CCT2 is identified as a single-gene marker of a translation-activated molecular state in sporadic ALS motor neurons, offering a candidate biological stratifier for a genetically heterogeneous disease.
  5. Sex-dependent DNA methylation in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis — Kim, Y. J. et al.
    A large epigenome-wide meta-analysis finds sex-dependent ALS methylation signals at immune, metabolic and ion-channel loci invisible to sex-stratified analyses alone.
  6. REFinder: Mining new enzymes from metagenomes — Prabakaran, R. et al.
    REFinder uses a DNA language model to triage metagenomic reads before assembly, recovering thousands of novel, homology-invisible enzymes far more cheaply than full-community assembly.
  7. A ribosomal pseudouridine drives an oncogenic translation program — Faucher-Giguere, L. et al.
    A single snoRNA-guided rRNA pseudouridine modification is shown to selectively reprogram translation of cancer-related mRNAs in ovarian cancer cells via a 'sno-balling' amplification cascade.
  8. Loss of the Y chromosome drives basal identity and metastatic potential via epigenetic reprogramming in pancreatic cancer — Dorsch, M. et al.
    Loss of the Y chromosome is identified as a recurrent driver of EMT and metastatic basal identity in pancreatic cancer through epigenetic reprogramming, affecting about half of male PDAC patients.
  9. Placental cis-eQTL analysis identifies preeclampsia-dependent genetic regulation at promoters — Yazgeldi Gunaydin, G. et al.
    Promoter-level, but not gene-level, cis-eQTL analysis in placenta reveals preeclampsia-dependent genotype interactions missed by standard gene-level eQTL mapping.
  10. An androgen-derived transcriptional state reveals signaling and mitochondrial vulnerabilities in cancer — Miao, Y. et al.
    An androgen-derived transcriptional signature, projected across cancer cell lines, reveals unexpected EGFR-resistance and mitochondrial dependency relationships independent of cancer lineage.

item.title: Wed Oct 7: Sparse model discovery for gene oscillators, identifiable optimal transport for cell transitions, and why spatial RNA and protein disagree on checkpoint markers
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. RI-SINDy: Regulation-Informed Sparse Model Discovery in Biological Gene Networks — Lucenti, N. J. et al.
    Introduces RI-SINDy, a sparse model-discovery method that removes collinear Hill-type regulatory terms before regression, substantially improving recovery of gene regulatory network dynamics from oscillatory time-series data like Hes1 and NF-kB.
  2. Identifiable inverse optimal transport for single-cell state transitions — Dong, H. et al.
    Proposes a semi-relaxed inverse optimal transport framework (UOT-IOT) that restores identifiability of target-state programme effects in single-cell state transitions, with strong gains over balanced OT on real perturbation and lineage data.
  3. RNA and protein are not interchangeable in single-cell spatial multi-omics — Cervilla, S. et al.
    A rigorous paired Xenium RNA/protein comparison across ~1.8M cells showing spatial organization is far more discordant between modalities than abundance, a cautionary result for anyone treating spatial transcriptomics as a protein proxy.
  4. MERFISH-based pooled genetic screening reveals cell non-autonomous phenotypes in intact tissue — Jin, K. et al.
    An amplification-free MERFISH pooled screening method that jointly reads perturbation identity, transcriptome, and spatial neighborhood in intact tissue, revealing cell-non-autonomous effects of hepatocyte perturbations on immune and vascular niches.
  5. Circular Data Analysis for Spatial Omics — Shin, J. et al.
    A practical methods guide for handling circular/periodic quantities (circadian phase, cell-cycle position) in single-cell and spatial omics, with worked examples showing when standard linear or spatial models mislead.

Briefs

  1. Identifiability of a linear dynamical reaction-diffusion system with directed interactions from the second-order statistics of a single snapshot — Pirmin Schlicke
    Shows that directed cell-cell interaction structure in reaction-diffusion models (e.g., tumor-immune tissue) is recoverable from the wavenumber-dependence of a single spatial snapshot's second-order statistics, not from means or simple covariance.
  2. Conservation of gene co-expression networks and neuropsychiatric-neurological disease gene programs between mouse and human frontal cortex at single-cell resolution — Sun, Q.-Q. et al.
    Large-scale single-cell comparison of gene co-expression networks between mouse and human prefrontal cortex finds only modest single-gene partner conservation but strong module-level preservation, with implications for translating GRN findings across species.
  3. Genetic dissection of DNA damage response pathways reveals divergent modulation of PD-1 blockade response in colorectal cancer — Fece de la Cruz, F. et al.
    A systematic in vivo DDR gene screen shows pathway-specific (not uniform) effects on anti-PD-1 response in MSS colorectal cancer, identifying ATM inhibition as a rational immunotherapy-sensitizing combination.
  4. Linkage disequilibrium moderates how evolving genetic background shapes variant-level architecture — Lee, H. et al.
    A population-genetic model coupling variant evolution to linkage-disequilibrium background shows that frequency-dependent effect-size patterns can arise from demographic history alone, without invoking differential selection strength across populations.
  5. Intraindividual longitudinal changes of the proteome reveal dynamic markers of biological aging — Lermer, R. et al.
    A longitudinal (not just cross-sectional) plasma proteomic aging clock in >4,000 individuals links within-person risk-factor changes to age-acceleration transitions and mortality, with Mendelian randomization support for causal aging proteins.
  6. Integrative genetic and transcriptomic analysis identifies candidate genes and compounds for Fragile X syndrome and autism spectrum disorder — Zhang, W. et al.
    Integrates population genetics, twin discordance, and FMRP-QTL data to link Fragile X syndrome biology to idiopathic autism's polygenic architecture and prioritize repurposable compounds.
  7. Establishment and characterization of LNCaP-TR-BoM, a bone metastasis-derived prostate cancer cell line with an intermediate AR-attenuated phenotype — Chao, A. et al.
    scRNA-seq and RNAi screening in regenerating planarian eyes identifies DDR collagen receptors and TMEM132 adhesion factors as controllers of progenitor migration and self-organized organ assembly, a nice model for cell fate/differentiation trajectories.
  8. Spatially restricted bmp16 in an extra-embryonic syncytium promotes dorsoventral patterning — Couturier, H. et al.
    Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics of the zebrafish yolk syncytial layer uncovers a spatially restricted bmp16 program that patterns the dorsoventral axis from an extra-embryonic compartment, illuminating multinucleate signaling organization.
  9. ASTRA enables zero-shot super-resolution of spatial transcriptomics across capture geometries — Ye, J. et al.
    ASTRA is a cross-platform, zero-shot pretrained model for spatial transcriptomics super-resolution that generalizes across capture geometries (Visium HD, pseudo-Visium) without per-section retraining.
  10. Genomic SEM reveals shared genetic architecture and expands locus discovery for locomotor activity in heterogeneous stock rats — Chitre, A. S. et al.
    Compares Genomic SEM against standard meta-analysis for locus discovery of a heritable behavioral trait across heterogeneous rat cohorts, nearly quadrupling loci found versus pooled GWAS—a methods lesson applicable to multi-cohort omics integration.

Quick mentions

  1. A near-ubiquitous plasmid characterises Second Pandemic Yersinia pestis — Seersholm, F. V. et al.
    Pangenomic analysis of ancient Yersinia pestis genomes finds a near-ubiquitous cryptic plasmid unique to the Black Death-era Second Pandemic, potentially explaining its outsized mortality via expanded vector range.
  2. Genomic classification and immune profiling define mucosal melanoma — Shi, Y. et al.
    Multimodal profiling of 339 mucosal melanoma patients defines four genomic subtypes and implicates CD163+ macrophage-TIM3 signaling as an immunotherapy resistance mechanism.
  3. EPHA4 Regulates the Transition between Mesenchymal and Hybrid States in TNBC — Liu, W. et al.
    EPHA4 loss shifts triple-negative breast cancer cells from mesenchymal to hybrid E/M states, trading invasiveness for enhanced metastatic colonization capacity.
  4. Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF Inhibitor — Desaunay, M. et al.
    A Type 1 RAF inhibitor exploits fast on/off binding kinetics to achieve tumor-selective MAPK suppression in RAS/RAF-dimer-driven cancers while sparing normal tissue.
  5. SLC25A28 is a synthetic lethal vulnerability in nucleotide excision repair-deficient cancers — Yang, N. et al.
    CRISPR screening identifies SLC25A28 (mitochondrial iron transport) as a synthetic lethal target in nucleotide excision repair-deficient cancers, offering a non-platinum therapeutic avenue.
  6. HMGA2 Expression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Controls Tumor Microenvironment and Immunosuppression via IL1α — Yamamoto, N. et al.
    HMGA2 in basal pancreatic cancer cells drives an IL1a-mediated immunosuppressive fibroblast program, and blocking IL1 signaling improves tumor control with KRAS inhibitors.
  7. KRAS-driven metabolic reprogramming of enhanced MFSD2A-mediated lysophosphatidylcholine scavenging promotes survival and progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma — chen, y. et al.
    KRAS-driven upregulation of the lipid transporter MFSD2A enables pancreatic cancer cells to scavenge extracellular lysophosphatidylcholines, a targetable metabolic dependency.
  8. A map of RBP-miRNA regulatory connections for deciphering the mechanisms of transcriptome remodeling in cancer — Perron, G. et al.
    A pan-cancer map of RNA-binding protein regulation of miRNA activity identifies DDX55 as a suppressor of tumor-suppressive miR-29-3p function across many cancer types.
  9. Neural Petri flows for chemical reactions — Jose Eduardo Escrig Molina et al.
    Neural Petri Flow hard-wires conservation laws into a learnable chemical reaction model, achieving strong atom-mapping and reaction-outcome prediction without training data in some settings.
  10. CRISPR-Cas9 Editing of Myeloid Lectins Reveals Target-Dependent Transcriptional Remodeling in Tumor-Associated Macrophages — Trindade, G. et al.
    CRISPR knockout of myeloid lectins in primary monocyte-derived TAMs reveals lectin-specific, rather than uniform, immunometabolic transcriptional reprogramming, nominating CLEC6A for further study.

item.title: Tue Oct 6: Methylation-based TF activity, generalizing perturbation prediction, and two cancer spatial atlases
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. methylTFR: Computational quantification of transcription factor activity from DNA methylation — Gunduz, I. B. et al.
    methylTFR cleverly infers transcription-factor activity directly from DNA methylation patterns at binding sites, giving an interpretable regulatory readout that scales to sparse single-cell methylomes and resolves known immune/T-cell lineage regulators.
  2. PIE: Generalizing perturbation effects across unseen perturbations, contexts and datasets — Verma, R. et al.
    PIE reformulates perturbation-response prediction around population-level differential expression with auxiliary biological context, achieving large gains in generalizing to unseen cell contexts, perturbations and datasets—directly relevant to perturbation-seq modeling.
  3. Scalable and semi-automated Boolean network inference from multi-condition single-cell transcriptomes with scBOLT — Roncalli, T. et al.
    scBOLT turns multi-condition single-cell transcriptomes into tractable Boolean regulatory network inference via constraint-satisfaction, tackling the long-standing bottleneck of data-driven logical model construction at scale.
  4. Matched primary-metastasis single-nucleus and spatial profiling of leiomyosarcoma identifies antigen-presenting fibroblasts at the tumor-organ interface — Kuebler, A. et al.
    A rare matched primary-metastasis single-nucleus and spatial atlas of leiomyosarcoma reveals organ-specific malignant programs and a spatially organized antigen-presenting fibroblast niche at the tumor-organ interface, directly informing tumor heterogeneity and metastatic evolution questions.
  5. Spatial transcriptomics reveals tumour cell-intrinsic and microenvironmental features associated with survival in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma — Khan, M. A. A. K. et al.
    A 122-patient Xenium spatial transcriptomics study of ovarian cancer shows that bulk-profiling masks tumor-cell-intrinsic survival associations and that integrated tumor-microenvironment signatures stratify patient outcome, a strong methodological case for spatial over bulk analysis.

Briefs

  1. Slide-level batch structure limits histology-guided supervision of transcriptomic foundation models — McConnell, U. et al.
    Shows that slide-identity batch structure in spatial transcriptomics confounds histology-guided training of transcriptomic foundation models, a cautionary methods result for anyone building multi-omic representation learners.
  2. How many cells resolve a perturbation direction? A closed-form, control-aware cell quota for single-cell perturbation screens — Tran, L. T. H. et al.
    Derives a closed-form cell-count quota for resolving perturbation directions in single-cell screens, giving a practical statistical rule for experimental design in perturb-seq studies.
  3. PWK genetic background reprograms heterochromatin and malignant epithelial states in Neu-driven mammary tumors — Geng, R. et al.
    Shows that genetic background reshapes heterochromatin organization and malignant cell-state trajectories in a mammary tumor model, linking inherited variation to epigenomic tumor evolution.
  4. Metabolic rewiring induces a viral mimicry-mediated quiescence in glioblastoma — Chesnelong, C. et al.
    Identifies a polyamine-metabolism-driven viral-mimicry program that induces reversible dormancy in glioblastoma stem cells, connecting metabolic rewiring to innate immune signaling and therapy resistance.
  5. Mechanistic Decoding of Pharmacodynamic Intratumoral Heterogeneity: A Pan-Cancer Regulatory Framework — Ren, Z. et al.
    A pan-cancer multi-omic framework links 425 hub genes and regulatory mechanisms to intratumoral pharmacodynamic heterogeneity, turning descriptive single-cell drug-response heterogeneity into mechanistic, targetable hypotheses.
  6. Selection on cuticle color produces a genome-wide response that does not localize to known major genes in Drosophila — Ruckman, S. N. et al.
    An elegant evolve-and-resequence experiment in Drosophila shows a genome-wide polygenic selection response even for a trait with known major-effect genes, with a cautionary artifact (chorion-gene amplification) relevant to pool-seq methodology.
  7. Hidden but Expanding Sampling Bias Distorts Prokaryotic Genome Collections — Götsch, H. et al.
    Quantifies pervasive and worsening phylogenetic sampling bias in public prokaryotic genome databases and proposes a correction method, with implications for any comparative genomics or microbiome study relying on these resources.
  8. Organizing principles of the cellular electron economy — Millard, P. et al.
    Formalizes a genome-wide 'cellular electron economy' showing that carbon source and electron-sink capacity jointly and separably set metabolic flux, a conceptually clean systems-biology organizing principle validated across five microbes.
  9. DE-SWAN analysis of biomarker trajectories over the life course is highly sensitive to age distribution and model parameterization — Che, A. et al.
    A rigorous simulation study shows the popular DE-SWAN method for detecting aging-rate accelerations is highly sensitive to sample age-distribution and window choice, undermining prior claims of multiple aging 'waves'.
  10. On non-monotonic steady state response curves — Polly Y. Yu et al.
    Proves that stable non-monotonic dose-response curves require either an incoherent feedforward loop or combined positive/negative feedback, refining a long-standing systems-biology conjecture with applications to signaling and gene regulation motifs.

Quick mentions

  1. Reconstructing donor genotypes from scRNA-seq for downstream eQTL and HLA-TCR analysis — Kockelbergh, H. et al.
    scTAPAS reconstructs usable donor genotypes directly from scRNA-seq reads, enabling eQTL and HLA-TCR association analyses without separate genotyping.
  2. Explainable t-SNE for Single-Cell RNA-seq Data Analysis: A Cell-DrivenInformation Fusion Framework — Han, H. et al.
    A non-Euclidean, count-aware affinity framework (c-TSNE/c-UMAP) improves scRNA-seq embedding quality and scales to over a million cells while better preserving lineage marker genes.
  3. KSHV upregulates the long non-coding RNA PURPL via p73 to suppress p53 — Showgan, S. et al.
    KSHV hijacks p73 to upregulate the oncogenic lncRNA PURPL as a new mechanism for viral suppression of p53 in Kaposi sarcoma-associated lymphoma.
  4. Haplotype-phased, chromosome-level, annotated genome assembly of the soybean rust pathogen Phakopsora pachyrhizi — Greatens, N. F. et al.
    A new haplotype-phased, chromosome-level genome assembly of the soybean rust fungus provides a major resource for studying this devastating crop pathogen's biology and virulence.
  5. Community Detection from Aggregated Relational Data: Identifiability and Spectral Recovery — Andrew Davison et al.
    Establishes identifiability and spectral-recovery guarantees for community detection from compressed 'aggregated relational data' network surveys, relevant to network inference methodology generally.
  6. Notch1 and Notch2 receptors mediate the prosensory functions of the Notch ligand Jagged1 in the mammalian cochlea — Huang, H. et al.
    Notch1/Notch2 receptors are shown to mediate Jagged1's role in maintaining cochlear prosensory progenitors, clarifying a developmental signaling mechanism behind hair-cell formation.
  7. Assay coverage reshapes metabolic diagnosis and the interpretation of pathway disturbance — Fontaine, C. et al.
    A new humanized mouse model of the ARMS2 A69S AMD risk variant links it to retinal mitochondrial dysfunction, providing the first in vivo platform for a gene previously untestable in rodents.
  8. trFlow: ultrafast all-atom protein conformational ensemble generation via conditional flow matching — Xiang, C. et al.
    trFlow generates all-atom protein conformational ensembles via flow matching an order of magnitude faster than existing methods, useful for structural systems-biology applications.
  9. Evaluating in-context learning with prompting regimes for transformer-based synthetic health tabular data generation — Bertgren, A. et al.
    Benchmarks prompting strategies for transformer-based synthetic health tabular data generation, finding zero-shot learning trades privacy for fidelity with no model-size effect.

item.title: Mon Oct 5: Flow-matching perturbation prediction, an evolvable lineage recorder, and how DNA supercoiling controls transcriptional bursting
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction using energy-guided flow matching — Jianan Wei et al.
    scEGFlow introduces an energy-guided flow matching framework for single-cell perturbation prediction that generalizes to unseen conditions, directly advancing the core methodology of modeling perturbation responses at single-cell resolution.
  2. Creation of a High-Resolution, Continually Evolvable Lineage Tracer — Delgado, R. N. et al.
    SCRIBBLE is a prime-editing-based, continually evolvable lineage recorder that enables high-resolution multigenerational lineage tracing in complex tissue, a major advance for studying cell fate and differentiation trajectories.
  3. Topoisomerase-mediated resolution of negative DNA supercoiling sustains human transcription and gene activation — Lyu, J. et al.
    Using single-cell NOTE-seq2 and genomic perturbation, this study mechanistically links topoisomerase-mediated DNA supercoiling resolution to RNAPII pausing, transcriptional bursting, and enhancer-promoter looping dynamics.
  4. Inference on paths of yeast transcription pre-initiation complex assembly by model-based analysis of altered occupancy profiles — Novikova, E. A. et al.
    A quantitative, differential-equation-based framework scores candidate pre-initiation complex assembly paths from ChIP-seq occupancy data in yeast Mediator mutants, offering a rigorous model-based approach to transcription initiation regulation.
  5. A kinetic-aware approach to infer metabolic variations and flux using transcriptomics and metabolomics data — Zhu, H. et al.
    mmFEA is a Monte Carlo, Michaelis-Menten-kinetics-based framework for integrating transcriptomics and metabolomics to infer condition-specific metabolic flux changes, directly relevant to systems biology modeling of cellular processes.

Briefs

  1. Genome-wide mapping of endogenous topoisomerase cleavage complexes reveals TOP1 at the interface of DNA topological regulation and genome instability — Li, S. et al.
    A new pDAIP-seq method maps endogenous topoisomerase cleavage complexes genome-wide without poison stabilization, revealing TOP1cc as a key source of spontaneous DNA breaks and complementing the companion supercoiling paper.
  2. Cancer stem cell transcriptomic signatures reveal patient-to-patient heterogeneity emphasizing the need for patient-specific ovarian cancer targets — Jung, M. S. et al.
    Patient-derived ovarian cancer stem cell RNA-seq reveals that stemness/chemoresistance phenotypes are conserved but driven by largely patient-specific isoform-level programs, highlighting isoform resolution as essential for precision oncology.
  3. Method-dependent biases in cell type detection between single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing in the photosymbiotic acoel Praesagittifera naikaiensis — Nakamura, R. et al.
    A systematic scRNA-seq vs snRNA-seq comparison in a symbiotic acoel shows method-dependent biases in neural cell detection and symbiont read contamination, offering practical guidance for cell atlas construction in non-model organisms.
  4. Why rescue-based transcript ranking can mislead: normalization displacement and shared-control coupling in perturbation transcriptomics — Jamil, H. M. et al.
    A sharp methodological critique shows how normalization choice and shared-control coupling can create spurious 'rescue' signals in perturbation transcriptomics, a cautionary tale for differential expression interpretation.
  5. Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families — Hantao Lou et al.
    ImmuneAgent, a closed-loop multimodal AI system, achieves striking hit rates discovering broadly neutralizing antibodies from human B cell repertoires, including cross-reactive antibodies against unseen viral targets.
  6. Spatially coordinated RTK-ERK signaling dynamics shape osteosarcoma single-cell drug response in the lung microenvironment — Makkawi, R. et al.
    Live-cell imaging and dynamical modeling reveal spatially coordinated FGFR-ERK signaling drives adaptive drug resistance in osteosarcoma lung metastases, suggesting rational combination therapy targets.
  7. The ortholog of the Human T2D Risk Gene STEAP2 is Required for Glucose Stimulated Insulin Secretion in Mice — Hawthorne, A. et al.
    A conditional knockout mouse model mechanistically links the T2D risk gene STEAP2 to mitochondrial cristae morphology and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in beta-cells, illuminating a GWAS hit's cell biology.
  8. GGE: General-purpose deep meta-learning for classification of human transcriptomes with limited data — Yankovitz, G. et al.
    GGE applies deep meta-learning across thousands of transcriptomic prediction tasks to improve classification in label-scarce settings, a generalizable tool for small-sample bioinformatics problems.
  9. Multi-scale Transcriptional Characterization of HPV16 and HPV18 in Cervical Cancer: Host Pathway Alterations and Links With Viral Gene Expression Programs — Ishihara, M. A. et al.
    Multi-cohort transcriptional profiling reveals HPV16 and HPV18 cervical cancers diverge along distinct host pathway axes linked to viral gene expression programs, suggesting genotype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities.

Quick mentions

  1. Toward Controlling Biology with Language:Offline Learning of Prompt-Conditioned Interventions for Cells, Organoids, and Biobots — Nam H. Le et al.
    An offline-trained vision-language model learns to map natural-language instructions to interventions on xenobots, a surprising step toward natural-language control of living systems.
  2. X-Y divergence of house fly (Musca domestica) proto-sex chromosomes follows distinct evolutionary trajectories despite residing in the same genome — Son, J. H. et al.
    Chromosome-level assemblies of five house fly strains reveal strikingly different canonical and non-canonical modes of X-Y divergence occurring within a single genome.
  3. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells in AML adopt an NK-like program distinct from canonical exhaustion — Chu, Y. E. et al.
    Single-cell RNA/TCR profiling of AML bone marrow shows clonally expanded CD8 T cells adopt an NK-like program rather than classical exhaustion, challenging standard T-cell dysfunction paradigms in cancer.
  4. Post-transcriptional dysregulation precedes morphological transformation in chemically induced liver cancer — Izuogu, O. G. et al.
    Reanalysis of liver tumor genomes across mouse backgrounds shows splicing, circRNA, and RNA editing changes precede morphological transformation, establishing a durable pre-cancerous post-transcriptional phenotype.
  5. Auditing Protein-Protein Interaction Signals with Sparse Autoencoder Fingerprints — Zhu, W. et al.
    AuditPPI uses sparse autoencoder fingerprints to show that many protein-protein interaction predictors rely on contextual shortcuts like co-localization rather than true interface-specific signals.
  6. Integrating CSF and EV Proteomes Enhances Biomarker Discovery by Capturing Shared Variation Across Compartments — Brown, B. R. P. et al.
    An integrated matrix factorization of CSF and extracellular vesicle proteomes boosts Alzheimer's biomarker discovery from a modest cohort by capturing cross-compartment shared variation.
  7. Generating eukaryotic reference genome assemblies: Earth BioGenome Project quality standards and recommendations — Kerstin Howe (Wellcome Sanger Institute et al.
    The Earth BioGenome Project consortium formalizes community-wide quality standards for reference genome assembly, setting benchmarks relevant to any sequencing-based analysis.
  8. A global signature of microbiome resilience to climate stress — Rawstern, A. et al.
    A large-scale analysis of ~29,000 microbiomes identifies network and functional properties that predict resilience to climate stressors, proposing a baseline sequencing-based early-warning framework.
  9. A coupled geometric surface and surface reaction-diffusion framework for modelling nuclear mechanics during confined cell migration — Francesca Ballatore et al.
    A coupled surface mechanics and reaction-diffusion model links chromatin-regulating enzyme balance to nuclear deformation dynamics during confined cell migration.
  10. Downstream mRNA Secondary Structure, Not Codon Elongation Supply, Coordinates Co-Translational Protein Folding Across the Human Ribosomal Exit Tunnel — Saad Ul Hassan, M. et al.
    Structural proteome analysis suggests downstream mRNA secondary structure, not codon-supply kinetics, subtly paces co-translational protein folding at a ribosome-geometry-matched offset.

item.title: Fri Oct 2: Metacells meet random matrix theory, why Wilcoxon markers lie, and saturation mutagenesis at scale
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. A Metacell Model of Single Cell RNA-seq Counts Yields a Gaussian Mixture Model in PCA Space — Leviyang, S.
    Provides the first theoretical link between a generative count model (metacells) and the ubiquitous PCA-embedding workflow in scRNA-seq, showing it yields a Gaussian mixture and exposing where real data deviate from this prediction.
  2. Limitations of differential expression for cell-type marker discovery in single-cell RNA sequencing atlases — Doggett, K. et al.
    A rigorous critique showing that the Wilcoxon test routinely used in Seurat/Scanpy for marker gene discovery is confounded by cluster size, with major implications for how atlas-scale cell-type annotation is done.

item.title: Thu Oct 1: Splicing factor mutations poisoning protein complexes in leukemia, a dosage-constrained EBF3 dependency, and CDX2's reused enhancers in gut regeneration
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. RNA splicing factor mutations drive myeloid neoplasm oncogenesis through protein complex poisoning — Moura, P. L. et al.
    Combines long-read single-cell transcriptomics with low-cell proteomics to show that splicing-factor mutations in myeloid neoplasms act by poisoning whole protein complexes, a mechanism invisible to transcriptomics alone and directly relevant to multi-omic integration methods.
  2. Tumor suppressor-like mutations mark a dosage-constrained dependency in leukemia — Lee, J. D. et al.
    Elegant reframing of cancer genetics showing that oncogene-driven dosage constraints can generate heterozygous loss-of-function mutations that mimic tumor-suppressor signatures while marking an essential dependency, with direct implications for how cancer genomes are interpreted.
  3. Pangenome-resolved polymorphic transposable elements reveal human regulatory evolution in action — Jiang, J. et al.
    A 231-haplotype pangenome resource resolving segregating transposable-element alleles as sequence, epigenetic state and transcript, revealing regulatory evolution 'in action' before fixation—a major resource for gene-regulatory and population genomics.
  4. CDX2 Drives Divergent Regional Programs During Intestinal Development and Redeploys Them During Regeneration — Lorzadeh, A. et al.
    Dissects how a single uniformly-expressed TF (CDX2) builds a hierarchical, region-specific enhancer network during development and redeploys distinct enhancer subsets during regeneration—core gene-regulation/chromatin biology.
  5. CellMSA: Context Modeling for Single-Cell Representation Learning — Suyuan Zhao et al.
    Proposes an MSA-inspired cross-cell context modeling architecture for single-cell foundation models trained on ~109M cells, directly addressing batch-effect and representation-learning challenges central to the field.

Briefs

  1. Accurate and scalable demultiplexing of single-cell RNA sequencing using BEACON — Ji, B. W. et al.
    A new demultiplexing method (BEACON) that learns background noise distributions to improve scRNA-seq sample classification accuracy, including multimodal protein-transcriptome applications.
  2. ProxiNet transfers spatially learned cellular proximity to dissociated single-cell transcriptomes — Zhan, Y. et al.
    ProxiNet transfers spatially-learned cell-proximity signatures to dissociated scRNA-seq data, recovering tissue organization and neighborhood structure without spatial coordinates.
  3. CHACAM: a cell-cell interaction-guided hierarchical attention model for high-precision cell identity annotation of scRNA-seq data in early C. elegans embryogenesis — Chen, X. et al.
    A cell-cell interaction-guided hierarchical attention model resolves ambiguous sister-cell identities in C. elegans scRNA-seq embryo atlases using ligand-receptor and contact-map priors.
  4. CycloCross: Adversarial single-cell RNA-seq data translation across species — Hacquard, O. et al.
    CycloCross adapts CycleGAN for cross-species scRNA-seq translation without relying on one-to-one orthologs, enabling interpolation of germ-cell developmental states across mouse, macaque and human.
  5. Gene flux shapes diversity and evolution of the ancient 17q21.31 inversion polymorphism — Harringmeyer, O. S. et al.
    Single-cell sperm sequencing reveals that the 17q21.31 inversion polymorphism, long thought to suppress recombination, still permits gene conversion-mediated exchange that has shaped haplotype diversity for half a million years.
  6. Cell-of-origin shapes tumor subtype in BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer — Lev, T. et al.
    Shows that BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer subtype is determined by cell-of-origin (basal-myoepithelial vs luminal), reshaping prevention strategy thinking using single-cell atlases.
  7. Stress-recovery dynamics reveal a separatrix in transcriptomic landscapes across organs and aging — Xu, B. et al.
    Uses neural ODEs on multi-organ transcriptomic stress-recovery time courses to identify a separatrix governing whether aged tissue states can return to baseline, a nice systems-biology application of dynamical systems theory.
  8. A moving target: non-stationary selection governs unsupervised prediction of viral fitness — Aris-Brosou, S. et al.
    A careful unsupervised benchmarking study shows that alignment-based models beat protein language models for viral fitness prediction, and traces this to non-stationary selection drifting site preferences over evolutionary time.
  9. Evo 2 as a classification machine: evidence from in-context learning and mechanistic interpretability — Bertolini Agnoletto, L. et al.
    Probes in-context learning and mechanistic interpretability of the Evo 2 genomic language model, finding scaling and perplexity are poor predictors of classification performance—useful cautionary methods result.
  10. Gene-family-dependent thermodynamic effects of oncogenic mutations on nucleosome-DNA binding stability: a comparative molecular dynamics study across 22 cancer hotspots — Freudenberger, S. et al.
    Molecular dynamics across 22 cancer hotspots reveals gene-family-specific thermodynamic signatures (RAS stabilizing vs kinase destabilizing) at nucleosome-DNA interfaces, linking chromatin biophysics to mutation hotspots.

Quick mentions

  1. Pervasive Somatic Mutations in NF1 Drive Cell Type and Spatially Specific Clonal Selection in Neurofibromatosis — Snellings, D. A. et al.
    Single-cell genomics across >1.7M cells shows pervasive, lineage-specific second-hit NF1 mutations in oligodendrocyte lineage cells that clonally expand before overt tumorigenesis.
  2. Bridging the gap between omics and structural data: A framework for interpreting protein-RNA interaction specificity — Fauconnet, Y. et al.
    Benchmarks AlphaFold3 against omics-derived binding preferences for protein-RNA interfaces, finding signs of sequence memorization rather than true specificity learning.
  3. Phylodynamic analysis reveals asymmetric and accelerating global spread of dengue virus — Hill, V. et al.
    Large-scale phylodynamic analysis of dengue genomes reveals asymmetric, accelerating global spread driven by travel volume rather than climate.
  4. Whole-genome characterization of Plasmodium falciparum population structure and drug resistance across Uganda and neighboring countries — Kiyaga, S. et al.
    National whole-genome survey of Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum reveals emerging multi-drug resistance haplotypes and cross-border parasite connectivity.
  5. Prion-induced heritable states in Caenorhabditis elegans — Ilbay, O. et al.
    Demonstrates that a yeast prion domain can confer heritable, reversible epigenetic states in C. elegans, extending protein-based inheritance beyond unicellular systems.
  6. The Metabolic Organ Clock: A Computable Framework Linking Cell-Lineage Architecture to Emergent Organ Bioenergetics — Martin Sevilla, A. et al.
    Proposes a computable framework linking cell-lineage tree topology to organ-level metabolic rate, finding terminal fate identity (not developmental depth) best predicts bioenergetics.
  7. A genome-scale ORF screen for resilience factors that protect the RPE and restore vision in aged mice — Lu, Y. R. R. et al.
    A genome-scale ORF screen identifies NKX2-5 as a reengineerable resilience factor that restores vision and reduces frailty in aged mice.
  8. Reducing growth-medium complexity reveals nutrient-responsive programs in a near-minimal bacterium — Duval, A. et al.
    A new serum-free defined medium for the near-minimal bacterium Mesoplasma florum reveals substantial nutrient-responsive transcriptional reprogramming useful for systems/synthetic biology.
  9. EsViritu is a sensitive and specific profiler for viral pathogen detection and genome recovery in metagenomes — Tisza, M. J. et al.
    EsViritu is a new taxonomic profiler for viral metagenomics that outperforms existing tools on sensitivity and specificity for pathogen detection and genome recovery.
  10. digestome: a licence-clean marker-gene panel for functional profiling of anaerobic digestion microbiomes — Päll, T.
    digestome offers a license-free marker-gene panel for functional profiling of anaerobic digestion microbiomes, useful for biogas operators needing open-licence alternatives to KEGG/MetaCyc.

item.title: Wed Sep 30: Untangling GRN circularity, timing whole-genome duplication bursts, and why deep learning still can't predict disease expression
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Interpretable machine learning coupled to gene regulatory networks uncovers subcircuits underlying cell fate decisions — Rarani, Z. H. et al.
    FOCAL couples interpretable machine learning with state-specific gene regulatory networks to prioritize causal TF-gene subcircuits driving cell fate decisions, directly addressing the core methodological challenge of moving GRN inference beyond topology-based circularity.
  2. Complete timing of copy-number amplification histories reveals whole-genome duplication dynamics and coincident oncogene amplification bursts — Gulhan, D. C. et al.
    Tau provides a rigorous mathematical framework to fully enumerate and time copy-number gain histories, revealing that whole-genome duplication opens a burst window for oncogene amplification rather than being a passive doubling event.
  3. Genomic correlates of metastatic competence and progression in human melanoma — Chatziioannou, E. et al.
    A large prospective melanoma cohort with matched primary-metastasis sequencing and spatial transcriptomics identifies a copy-number signature (OncoCycle) that predicts relapse, showing metastatic competence is primed by chromosomal instability rather than point mutations.
  4. The strength of a gene's first 5' splice site is a key determinant of its expression — Sakai, Y. et al.
    A large-scale reporter screen reveals that intron-mediated enhancement of gene expression is governed by the strength of a gene's first 5' splice site independent of splicing efficiency, a fundamental and unexpected rule of gene regulation with implications for interpreting expression-altering variants.
  5. Disease relevance and replicability of deep learning gene expression prediction — Zhang, A. et al.
    A critical re-evaluation shows that popular deep learning models for predicting gene expression from DNA sequence mainly capture binary on/off status rather than disease-relevant expression changes, a sobering methodological finding for anyone using these models for regulatory genomics.

Briefs

  1. An agentic AI environment to support biomedical research in collaborative academic environments — Wu, T. et al.
    EpiZoo is a 2.6B-parameter DNA-sequence-aware foundation model trained on ~21M cells across species that enables cross-species comparative chromatin accessibility analysis and cancer mutation prioritization.
